cities.d: known as the "City of Smiles" because of the MassKara Festival (Máscara in Spanish) held annually on October 19, it is one of the gateways to Negros Island and the home of the famous Bacolod Chicken…

x.around: Most local transport within the city and to nearby towns is by jeepney, though taxis, ride-hailing services, buses, and rental cars are also available. The streets follow a rough grid in the downtown core, but become less orderly farther out. Traffic has increased with the city’s growth and is common during rush hour, especially in the early evening as commuters head home.

hidden.d: Marks the site where Pope John Paul II celebrated Mass for thousands of Bacolodnons.

This relatively new church is dedicated to St. Jude Thaddeus, patron saint of lost causes. It is notable for its richly decorated, gold-toned Baroque-style altar, ceiling mural, and Divine Mercy shrine.

This private display is the result of many years of collecting figurines and related items. Its miniature Christmas village features intricate hand-painted details, including cliffs, lakes, and mountains, all made by the owner.
A movement of concerned citizens to conserve the forests of Negros Island as well as animals that are under threat of extinction.

n.en: Negros Forests and Ecological Foundation Inc.

hidden.d: A university museum with exhibits ranging from indigenous woven textiles, plantation-era furniture, religious vestments, santos, and other devotional objects to rotating works by local and international artists on social,…
The park surrounding the stadium is filled with eucalyptus trees.

x.intro: Bacolod is the capital of the province of Negros Occidental in the Philippines and the most populous city on Negros Island. It is known for its MassKara Festival, a Mardi Gras-like parade and spectacular mix of dancing, colour and music held every October, as well as for its culinary heritage that includes inasal (a kind of roast chicken on skewers) and sweet dessert treats.

must.d: Bacolod’s main Catholic church, begun in the late 19th century and completed in 1894. Built of coral stone and later covered with cement, it is one of the city’s key landmarks.

The Bacolod version of Central park but smaller; fountains are scattered around the plaza and a gazebo stands in the middle. The Unknown Soldiers Monument (also known as Theodore Vinther Monument) is found here.

next.d: known as the Paris of Negros because of its European styled hundred year-old houses which are well preserved as historical monuments
and Bago – mountain resorts and hot springs
popular for divers and tourists alike
whale and dolphin watching
a popular university city with a clean seaside boulevard and a laid-back atmosphere
taste its mangoes, which are known to be among the sweetest in the world
the largest and most vibrant city on Panay

x.safe: Bacolod is safer than Metro Manila, but petty theft can still happen. Be particularly careful in the downtown/CBD and during the MassKara Festival, when crowds make pickpocketing easier. Keep valuables out of sight, carry only what you need, and use a taxi or ride-hailing service late at night rather than walking in quiet areas.

cities.d: Luzon's summer capital because of its cool weather, it boasts well-maintained parks and scenic areas, and is the home of the "Igorot", the indigenous peoples of the Cordilleras.

x.around: Similar to Manila, jeepneys ply various routes within Baguio and its immediate surroundings. Majority of jeepneys going out of the city (P.M.A., Country Club, etc.) are stationed in Burnham Park where they normally load passengers to their destinations. It is possible to a rent a jeepney but it is not advisable when trekking long distances.

hidden.d: Enjoy the view of the beautiful mountain scenery with other various attractions... And that's just it. This place is more of a tourist trap.
Massive artwork made up of a tightly packed cluster of hillside homes painted in bold colors.

A contemporary stone attraction made through the traditional method of riprap and reinforced with concrete. Made from the concept of an Igorot child's fantasy of castles, the Igorot Stone Kingdom is meant to showcase Igorot…
This family-friendly outdoor space has trees, flowers & stone sculptures, plus a butterfly preserve.
Ethnographic museum.
one of the best panoramic sights in Baguio City.
Popular botanical garden featuring a variety of plants & colorful flowers, along with native huts.

x.intro: Baguio is a highland city of 366,358 people (2020 census) in the province of Benguet, Philippines. Due to its cool mountain weather relative to the rest of the country, it is considered the "Summer Capital of the Philippines." The city is abundant in pine trees, so it is nicknamed the City of Pines.

must.d: Located at Fort Gregorio del Pilar on Loakan Road, visitors Philippine Military Academy History, Traditions & General Information to the City of Pines are welcome to explore the grounds, view the cadets performing their drills,…

The main thoroughfare of Baguio, where most of the city activity is centered. SM Mall and Burnham Park are walking distance. Take a look at the cool robot sculptures and the mascots that sometimes pass by.

Limestone sculpture of a lion by the Baguio chapter of the Lions Club. It is carved by Ifugao artist Anselmo Bayang Day-ag and is considered as the Baguio's "entrance marker" for tourists coming from south of the city.
The President of the Philippines summer home features manicured lawns & gardens open to the public.
Considered to be haunted, this house built in the 1930s houses Filipino bamboo & wood artworks. After Dec 2022, the house has been turned into an upscale fine-dining restaurant called "Joseph's".
One of the most haunted place in the Philippines.

next.d: in Benguet is the highest mountain in Luzon (2922 MASL) and a very popular hiking destination with its stunning scenery and "sea of clouds" views of the Cordillera mountain range.

x.safe: As a number one rule, always secure your belongings. Keep your passports/visas/important papers at the hotel safe (if there is one available at your hotel) or in a safe place. Cellphone snatching and purse dippers are a problem but common sense and safety can keep you safe.

cities.d: known as the "City of Golden Friendship", it is popular for white water rafting and is the gateway to Northern Mindanao.

x.around: Jeepneys, multicabs, motorelas, taxis, trisikads and sidecars are the main modes of land transportation in Cagayan de Oro. Like other cities in the Philippines, CDO has its own share of traffic problems. The city experiences significant traffic congestion from 6 am to 8 am in the morning, between 11 am and 2 pm in the noon, and from 5 pm to 8 pm in the evening.

hidden.d: The museum was opened in 2008, but the water tower was completed in 1922, and survived World War II. It houses photos of people who contributed to Cagayan de Oro over the years, and life and events from yesteryear.

n.en: City Museum of Cagayan de Oro

hidden.d: The area surrounding the monastery is also the residence of several religious orders, including the Discalced Carmelites, as well as the St. John Vianney Theological Seminary.
Formerly the Archdiocesan Shrine of the Holy Eucharist, Santuario Eucaristico is a shrine dedicated to St. Peter Julian Eymard, Apostle of the Eucharist.

It was built in the early 1900s as a town divider (hence the name Divisoria) or fire breaker after a great fire that almost burned down the entire town. The park is dedicated to local and national heroes.

Its focal point is a statue of Jesus as the Divine Mercy overlooking Macajalar Bay. The site attracts many pilgrims every Divine Mercy Sunday, one week after Easter Sunday, as well as during solemnities and other feast days…
A museum of Philippine household heirlooms and antiques. This is the Rodolfo and Elsa Pelaez family memorabilia administered by Liceo de Cagayan University.
Exhibits artifacts dug from Huluga Cave, and a repertoire of Bukidnon and Maranao cultures that have survived the ravages of time.
A circular park named after Segundo Gaston, a former pre-war Municipal Mayor of Cagayan de Oro, and is a favorite place to unwind for many Kagay-anons, especially during Sundays.

x.intro: Cagayan de Oro, often abbreviated CDO and sometimes just called "Cagayan", is known as the "City of Golden Friendship." It is the capital of the Province of Misamis Oriental and the "Gateway of Northern Mindanao."

must.d: A Gothic-inspired cathedral and is the seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Cagayan de Oro, since it houses the cathedra (seat) of the Archbishop of Cagayan de Oro.

next.d: via Bukidnon

x.safe: CDO is almost certainly safer than much of Mindanao, but that does not mean it is entirely safe. See the Mindanao article for warnings that apply to the entire region.

cities.d: the "Queen City of the South" was the first Spanish base in the Philippines and is a major center for commerce, industry, culture and tourism; Metro Cebu is the country's second largest urban area,…

x.around: See the Metro Cebu article for a more general discussion of getting around in the large urban conglomerate of which Cebu City forms a part.

hidden.d: Paintings and sculptures by local artists and antiques donated by wealthy Cebuanos.
Another historic house, this one from the 17th century, with hand-carved furniture and a garden. It does indeed look old/cryptic.
Where you can go to see Lepidoptera and other entomology exhibits, including a butterfly and art garden, although it's pretty scrunched in to an urban environment.

n.en: Jumalon Butterfly Sanctuary And Art Gallery

hidden.d: Neo-grecian temple built onto the mountainside to memoralize Leah Villa Albino Adarna, the wife of a local entrepreneur family and grandmother of actress Ellen Adarna.
Small exhibit hall on Chinese heritage in Cebu. This building (the Gotiaoco Building), also has a mural of the Magellan's Cross shrine and other Cebu highlights on its backside.
The tallest building in the city. Adventure seekers may head to the top floor to experience a breathtaking view of this modern city and its environs.
Yet another heritage house museum, this one the residence of a Jesuit from around 1730. Inside looks like a Spanish galleon.

A well-preserved Spanish colonial mansion constructed largely of wood, set in a pleasant, manicured garden. The lower floor has a collection of old tools, and an A/C room that has changing displays such as art exhibitions.

x.intro: Cebu City is the main city on Cebu Island in the Philippines and is known as the Queen City of the South. It is the capital of Cebu Province, a transport hub, and a popular tourist destination in its own right.

must.d: A large and venerable church that traces its history to the founding of the convent of the Santo Niño de Cebu in 1565.
The smallest Spanish outpost in the Philippines during the colonial era. It has a small museum showcasing the wreckage and treasures from the sunken San Diego galleon from Mexico.
A church built in 1565 by the first Spanish missionaries in Cebu, seat of an Archbishop who has subordinate Bishops in many cities of the Visayas.

An octagonal building decorated with murals containing a large wooden cross that commemorates the Portuguese conquistador Ferdinand Magellan who planted a wooden cross upon converting the original inhabitants to Christianity.

Brave the cacophonous traffic to see the oldest street in the Philippines with some nice worn-out classical buildings dating back to the American Era. At night, this street transforms into a market with good buys everywhere.
There are many people of Chinese ancestry in Cebu, and several Chinese temples; one is the Taoist Temple. From there you can see a nice view of the city because it is on a hill.

The museum is housed in the former Cebu Provincial Detention and Rehabilitation Center, which was once the Carcel de Cebu. Its four Spanish-era buildings made of coral stone contain artifacts relating to the history of Cebu.

Particularly scenic at night, is by far the largest provincial capitol building anywhere in the entire archipelago. It was built during the American era, and the design is a miniature of the White House.

next.d: beach, bus 2½-3 hr from south bus terminal, + tricycle to beach around , a diving destination with generally moderate prices
fast ferry from Cebu city (to Poro port) or by Jomalia ferry from Danao to Consuelo port (bus from Cebu City, 1-2 hours).
Island, off to the north of Cebu island.
south of Cebu, known for whale shark watching, can be visited en route to Dumaguete
an island province east of Cebu, popular for its scenic Chocolate Hills and tarsiers.
capital of a neighboring province, with a relaxed bar scene and good diving nearby.
capital of a neighboring province and second-largest city in the Visayas, is reachable by taking a bus to Toledo, a ferry to San Carlos and then another bus.

x.safe: Cebu is a relatively safe city where violent crime is rare. This being said, you should be aware of your surroundings.

cities.d: the largest city in the Philippines in terms of land area, is known for its durian fruit and for being the home of Mount Apo, the Philippines' tallest mountain.

x.around: Taxis start their fare at ₱45 and will add per few hundred meters. Please do say "thank you" or "salamat" once you have arrived at your destination. Davao Taxis issue fare receipts that list the name of the taxi company, the plate number, and the taxi number which could come in handy if one leaves valuable items or documents inside a cab. Just tell your taxi driver if you want to get a receipt.

hidden.d: See the Philippine eagle, one of the largest eagles in the world, and one of the most endangered. The center is home to about 30 Philippine eagles.
This cathedral, built in the 19th century, is the city's main cathedral. It is across from City Hall.

The park serves as a breeding center of crocodiles and houses also a small zoo, with daily animal shows on the central stage. Possibilities to feed crocodiles, tigers and some other animals for a fee.
This was a hangout for Japanese Forces during World War II. It is now a tourist spot in Davao City, where you can have a scenic view of Davao City (especially during the night).
No photos except on few recent paintings and a separated room.
A shrine that is up a hill with views across Davao in which you can unwind, relax, and reflect. There are mass celebrations once in a while per day. A lot of people visit this place during Sundays.

n.en: Shrine of the Holy Infant of Jesus

hidden.d: A public park located along Legazpi Street. A park where people people gather around, enjoy the stroll crossing bridges,exercising around the walkway which circles the park, seeing man-made waterfalls, beautiful plants, etc.

x.intro: Davao is the largest city on the Philippines' second-largest island, Mindanao. It has a huge land area, and the inhabitants like to think of it as one of the most crime-free large cities in the Philippines.

must.d: The highest mountain in the Philippines, a dormant volcano.

next.d: 66 km south of Davao, 1½ hours by bus
4-5 hours by bus
bus/van 7-10 hours, depending on weather, traffic and road construction. Stops including lunch+dinner break.
149 km, 3-4 hours by bus
city: 6-7 hours by bus/van
5-6 hours by bus/van
3-4 hours by bus/van
6 hours by bus

x.safe: Because of the work of the local government on strengthening security during the past decade Davao is generally a safe city even for travellers and violent crime is rare except a few parts of downtown Davao are unsafe at night. Armed guards and security forces can be seen everywhere, guarding malls, hotels and public events.

intro: The Philippines (Filipino: Pilipinas), officially the Republic of the Philippines (Republika ng Pilipinas), is an archipelago of more than 7,100 islands in Southeast Asia.

other.d: has 2,000-year-old rice terraces and called by Filipinos the eighth wonder of the world, it is a . People are fascinated at the immense work of the Igorots (mountain tribes of northern Luzon) in…

x.around: Jeepneys (converted jeeps/bus) and tricycles (trikes) (little motorcycles with side cars) are easily available around Banaue. Vans can be hired with driver/guide. Expect to hike some to great places to see that are not on the roads.

hidden.d: Breath taking views and friendly shop keepers.
A geothermal hot spring next to a river can be reached via walking across rice terraces starting from Hungduan Elementary School. The road to the school however is not yet paved.

The Museum of Cordilleran Sculpture was founded by George and Candida Ida Schenk over 30 years ago, and evolved from a small antique store in Manila, into dream to preserve a culture that is slowly dying.

Natural history museum. Very small museum. Interesting things to see about Ifugao Culture, attire, handicraft, etc. Good to visit. High steps/stairs to reach the entrance to the museum, then another stairs to the lower level.
Banaue Ethnic Village and Pine Forest Resort is on a six hectare lot in a pine forest above downtown Banaue. It has large grassy areas, picnic shelters, swimming pools, and a large function hall.

n.en: Banaue Ethnic Village and Pine Forest Resort

x.intro: Banaue is a town in the province of Ifugao in the Cordillera mountain range in the north of the island of Luzon, in the Philippines. It is mainly visited for its stunning rice terraces, which are designated a National Cultural Treasure.

must.d: Sometimes called the "Eighth Wonder of the World", the 2000-year-old Banaue rice terraces are a designated National Cultural Treasure, and while many are still in use, the outer rims are showing signs of deterioration.

n.es: Arrozales en terrazas de las cordilleras de Filipinas

next.d: . While the rice terraces of Banaue are mud-walled, those of Batad are stone-walled. They form an amphitheatre and are an impressive sight.
A major city that has several bus route through on their way north from Manila. Ohayami Trans has a daily trip to Baguio at 5:30PM and takes about 9 hr for + fees
Ohayami Trans has a daily trip to at 7PM and takes about 9 hr. Alternatively, you can get a jeepney to the junction just before Solano and catch a Manila bound bus - the bus will take around 8 hours…
. By hiring a van in Banaue (ask in your hotel) you can visit these two centres as a day trip. Bontoc is a busy town but has an excellent museum of Ifugao culture.

x.safe: Permits are required from local authorities to undertake most hikes or mountain climbing. The hiking season runs during the dry season from November to May. While Banaue is often known for its cool weather, do not underestimate the effects of heat and exhaustion while climbing, especially as many of the slopes are directly exposed to sunlight.

other.d: is a 10-km-long island featuring white sands, one of the country's best-known resort areas.

x.around: Most visitors opt for electric tricycles, which act as the island's taxis and make up most of its traffic. Rides are usually no more than for individual (per tricycle, not shared with other people) ride to any point on the island, and can be found almost anywhere along the main road. :From Cagban Port to Station 1, the most that you should pay is per head.

hidden.d: This is what most people are here for, but there are environmental rules and the beach is a challenge for people with disabilities.
Come there on a windy days to see kiteboarders doing high jumps and crazy tricks.
The biggest school on Boracay. Very passionate about kitesurfing and very professional.
A quiet stretch of white sand along the northern tip of the island, Puka Beach is an image of what most people expect on a tropical island: white sand, azure water, and relatively empty.

x.intro: Boracay is a tropical island about an hour's flight from Metro Manila in the Philippines. It has superb long white sand beaches and is one of the country's most developed tourist destinations.

next.d: the closest major airport is in this town
largest city on Panay

x.safe: Sewage water pollution is one of the biggest problems in Boracay: raw sewage is piped directly into the sea. Some areas, like Bulabog beach, have been made completely unswimmable due to this problem. However, it puts the swimming safety of the entire island under serious threat.

other.d: is the Whale Shark Capital of the world, dive and see whale sharks.

x.around: There are lots of tricycles in Donsol that will get you wherever you want. To go from the city center to Dancalan the price is for 2 people.
x.intro: Donsol is a municipality in the province of Sorsogon, Philippines. It's known for the eco-tourism activity involving an interaction with the whale sharks.

next.d: via Masbate

other.d: has dozens of limestone islands that form a stunningly beautiful karst topography permeated by crystal-clear bays and lagoons, still relatively unspoiled by mass tourism

x.around: The easiest way to see the Bacuit Bay is on an island hopping boat. These boats carry 6-12 people and will visit 4 or 5 destinations in a day. These destinations include: secret beaches, blue or green lagoons, various islands, and amazing natural land-formations. The boats usually take set routes named A to D, but can vary depending on tides and weather.

hidden.d: This small dive center will offer you relaxing and long dives (departure at 8AM, come back at 4:30PM) among the colourful aquatic life of Bacuit Bay.

x.intro: El Nido is a coastal town in Palawan. El Nido comprises 45 islands and islets; limestone cliffs are also found here, which form a Karst backdrop similar to those found in Ha Long Bay, Krabi and Guilin. It is a popular destination for locals during the long holidays of the Holy Week, but has been relatively unknown to foreign tourists. El Nido is more than just a stereotypical tropical paradise.

next.d: diving hotspot, with abundant sealife and many Japanese WWII wrecks

other.d: Island features a beautiful white sand shoreline and coral gardens.

x.around: There is no transport on the island — not that you will need any, as you can walk everywhere.

hidden.d: PADI Diving courses from beginner to professional. Especially for SPANISH Divers .Diving in small groups with experienced divemasters in a fun environment. More 10 years experience on Malapascua and Divemasters.

x.intro: Malapascua is an island in Cebu Province north of Cebu Island. The first image Malapascua offers will stay with you for a long time: an exceedingly beautiful pristine stretch of white sand, crystal clear waters bordered by coconut trees and a dozen scattered native-style resorts. But as with all up-and-coming islands experiencing a boom in tourism, Malapascua is rapidly becoming a second Boracay with modern concrete hotels to cater for the varied needs of the many.
x.safe: There is a basic clinic on Malapascua Island, close by to the Barangay Hall. A doctor comes only every Saturday to Malapascua's little clinic. So to help in case of an emergency injuries outside of a Saturday, one still has to go to the next doctor in Daanbantayan, and that is long way by boat and land transport.
